title: Moving as little as possible
summary: Pick each next voicing so your fingers barely move.

steps.title: Voice leading
steps.body:
Each finger in a chord is like a singer holding one note. Moving from chord to chord so each "singer" moves as little as possible is called **voice leading**. C (C E G) to F is smoothest as C F A: C stays, E steps up to F, G steps up to A.

**Why it matters:** Good voice leading is why a band keyboard player sounds smooth instead of jumpy, and it keeps your hand in one place on the keyboard.

steps.title: C to G, smoothly
steps.body: C E G to B D G: G stays, C steps down to B, E steps down to D.

items.prompt: Play C, E and G together.
Move to F with as little movement as you can: play the chord written F/C.
Now move to G the smooth way: play the chord written G/B.

steps.title: Find the short way
steps.body: Play C, then find the F nearest your hand, then the G nearest that. Count how many fingers move each time.

items.prompt: From A, C and E, move to F the smooth way: play the chord written F/A.
From G, B and D, move to C the smooth way: play the chord written C/G.
